name: Standard Scramble

pitch_detail.notes: Steep heather, mossy slabs, brush, and short cliff bands; primary route-finding challenge
~100 vertical feet on looser, sandier rock; the exposed crux of the route

descent_text: Reverse the ascent line exactly. Downclimb the summit block using the same Class 2-3 moves in reverse — staying on the right (east/south) side is easier and less exposed than the left — then descend from the notch down the loose scree/talus couloir back to Chain Lakes camp (watch footing and any parties below you — this gully sheds rock easily), then follow Chain Lakes Trail #1569 downhill, pick up the Icicle Creek Trail, climb back up to the PCT junction, and follow the PCT north back to the Stevens Pass trailhead. This is a walk-off/downclimb descent with no rappelling on the standard route: 0 rappels. Note that a separate, harder line on the same peak — the technical South Ridge route used by parties doing the full Bullseye Traverse, which ropes up for Class 4-5.8 climbing to reach the true summit gap between Bull's Tooth and the adjacent 'Bullfinch' pinnacle — does use two to three short (~20-30 ft) rappels off horns, trees, and slung blocks to get back down that exposed ridge crest; that gear/anchor style does not apply to the standard scramble described here, which avoids the technical ridge entirely via the couloir and a downclimb.
approach: Start at the Stevens Pass PCT-South trailhead (large lot on the south side of US 2, ~4,060 ft, just east of the ski area buildings). Follow the Pacific Crest Trail south; the trail climbs gradually through forest and past Lake Susan Jane, staying high above Nason Creek before working into the Icicle Creek drainage. At roughly 4.5-5 miles from the trailhead, watch for the signed junction with the Icicle Creek Trail (leave the PCT here). Follow the Icicle Creek Trail around Josephine Lake and down past its outlet, about 3.2 miles, to the junction with Chain Lakes Trail #1569. Turn onto Chain Lakes Trail and climb steeply — about 2.5 miles and 1,800-2,000 ft of gain through forest, brush, and talus benches — to the Middle/Upper Chain Lakes basin (~5,700 ft), the last reliable water and the standard base camp for the peak; tank up here, as there is no dependable water above the lakes. From camp, leave the maintained trail and go cross-country around the north/west shore of Upper Chain Lake, then ascend the huge white talus of the northwest-facing gully on the peak's west side to a notch between two sub-summits — footing is loose here and rockfall onto parties below is a real hazard, so group up in the gully. From the notch, scramble south to the base of the summit block. The final pitch to the top is Class 2-3 scrambling on solid granite; the easiest line works around the right (east/south) side of the summit block rather than the left, finishing with an exposed but short Class 3 step and mantle onto the summit. Beyond Chain Lakes the route is entirely unmarked cross-country travel, so route-finding competence, a map/GPX track, and comfort on loose talus and heather slopes are required; the upper mountain is fully exposed to afternoon thunderstorms with no bail-out shelter.
overview: Bulls Tooth is a striking granite summit on the arcuate ridge rimming Chain and Doelle Lakes in the Chiwaukum Mountains, about 5.5 miles southeast of Stevens Pass in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness (Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest). It's one of the longest approaches out of Stevens Pass -- roughly 10 miles one-way via the PCT, Icicle Creek Trail, and the steep, unswitchbacked Chain Lakes Trail (#1569) -- rewarding backpackers with a quiet basin and a short, airy Class 3 scramble to a broad summit point. Note there is long-standing disagreement over which nearby point is 'the' Bulls Tooth: the name is mapped to a 6,807-ft triangulated point, applied to this higher 6,840+ ft high point (the one described in this route), and reserved by some locals for a lower, more fang-shaped 6,680+ ft summit near the Chain-Doelle pass that requires roped Class 4-5 climbing and a rappel. Runoff from the basin drains into Icicle Creek, a major tributary of the Wenatchee River.
beta: Bulls Tooth has no maintained summit trail. Parties reach the base via the Chain Lakes basin — a scenic, blueberry-covered alpine bench in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness — then climb through steep heather, mossy slabs, brush, and short cliff bands to boulder fields below the summit block, finishing on a short, exposed Class 3 pitch of looser, sandier rock near the top. Route-finding is the main challenge; there is no cairned or established line.
face: North/notch side of the summit block
